# The Second Heavy-Ball Riddle

> Research notes on convergence beyond the prescribed Lyapunov family.

## Canonical URLs

- Blog: https://trace231.github.io/heavyball-blog/
- Full PDF: https://trace231.github.io/heavyball-blog/heavyball-notes.pdf

## Summary

These research notes study the second Heavy-Ball riddle for smooth strongly convex optimization. They exhibit an exact normalized parameter witness where the prescribed two-point linear/quadratic Lyapunov family fails, while no nonconstant finite cycle exists in any finite dimension. They also state a uniform global linear convergence result throughout an explicit parameter box around that witness.

## Main results

- The exact witness is (q*, a*, b*) = (1/100, 113/50, 3/5).
- The prescribed two-point certificate family fails at the witness.
- Every nonconstant finite Heavy-Ball cycle is excluded at the witness.
- An explicit box of radius 10^-5 around the witness has a uniform global linear convergence guarantee.
- The obstruction is informational: a common finite-valued energy using only a two-point record cannot encode all objective-dependent future behavior.

## Scope and status

This is a draft research-note placeholder. The complete proof, arithmetic checks, figures, and review records are in the PDF. The project does not currently provide a Lean kernel-checked formalization; publication review and priority assessment remain separate from the internal verification record.

## Suggested retrieval terms

Heavy-Ball method, smooth strongly convex optimization, Lyapunov certificate, finite cycles, interpolation constraints, global linear convergence, two-point record energy, Zames-Falb multiplier.
